Right knee pain and locking for 6 months, worsening despite conservative treatment.
Mr. Rodriguez sustained a right knee injury 6 months ago while playing soccer. Initial
injury included swelling and pain. Over the past 6 months, he has experienced persistent
pain, mechanical symptoms (locking, catching), and functional limitations affecting his
ability to work and participate in recreational activities.

4. Intra-articular cortisone injection - 2 months ago, provided temporary relief

M23.201 - Derangement of unspecified meniscus due to old tear or injury, right knee
Clinical of Patient: Miguel Rodriguez | DOB: 11/22/1978 | MRN: MRN789012 I Date: 01/16/2024
Mr. Rodriguez has a complex medial meniscus tear with persistent mechanical symptoms
despite 6 months of comprehensive conservative treatment. He is an appropriate candidate
1. MRI confirmed complex medial meniscus tear - Non-repairable tear pattern
2. Persistent mechanical symptoms - Locking and catching episodes
3. Failed conservative treatment for 6 months - Including PT, injections, bracing
4. Functional limitations affecting daily activities - Unable to return to sports
5. Positive clinical tests - McMurray and Appley grind tests
6. Ongoing pain and effusion - Despite optimal medical management
Procedure: Right knee arthroscopy with partial medial meniscectomy and chondroplasty
Approach: Standard arthroscopic portals (anteromedial and anterolateral)
Anesthesia: General anesthesia with regional block
Arthroscopic meniscectomy is medically necessary due to failed conservative treatment,
persistent mechanical symptoms, and functional limitations. The procedure is indicated per
AAOS guidelines for complex meniscus tears with mechanical symptoms that have not
